title: Cap acceptances at 5 per WMBT; split the WMBT when more are needed

facts.note: Plan/WMBT/acceptance artifacts are identifiable by file kind and path.
Fires on authoring, revising or reviewing any WMBT or acceptance, including lists of five or fewer and edits to test mappings, metric_id, dimension, lens_ref or parent context.
Violation signal for the cap only, not an activation prerequisite; needs a counter of acceptances grouped by parent WMBT in the changed plan artifacts.

fires: A planner adds a sixth acceptance to an existing WMBT.
A planner drafts a new WMBT whose outcome seems to require more than five acceptances.
A planner reviews or revises a WMBT's acceptance list, even one with five or fewer acceptances.
A planner edits an existing acceptance's test mapping, metric_id, or the WMBT's dimension, lens_ref or inherited context.
doesNotFire: Implementation or test-code changes that do not touch planning artifacts.
Editing documentation unrelated to WMBTs or acceptances.

given: A WMBT and its acceptances in a plan.
when: The planner authors, revises or reviews the WMBT or any of its acceptances.
then: Keep at most 5 acceptances per WMBT (acceptance_cap max = 5); if more are needed, split the WMBT into clearer outcomes instead of exceeding the cap.
prefer: Split an over-full WMBT into several WMBTs with clearer outcomes, each with <=5 acceptances.
Map each acceptance to exactly one test (acceptance_to_test 1:1); several tests may target one component (test_to_component N:1).
Give each acceptance exactly one metric_id.
Keep each WMBT to one dimension and one lens_ref; acceptances inherit context from the parent WMBT.
avoid: Exceeding 5 acceptances on a WMBT, or gaming the cap by merging independent checks into one compound acceptance.
Acceptances with mixed measures (more than one metric_id).
One acceptance spread across several tests, or several acceptances sharing one test.
Mixing dimensions or lens_refs within one WMBT.
why: A WMBT needing more than five acceptances usually hides several outcomes; the cap keeps each WMBT one clear outcome with one measure and one test per acceptance.
evidence: Count acceptances per parent WMBT in the plan: every WMBT has <=5.
Each acceptance references exactly one metric_id.
Each acceptance maps to exactly one test; tests may share a component (N:1).
Each WMBT declares one dimension and one lens_ref; acceptances inherit context from it.
verifier_detail: Threshold: max_per_wmbt = 5 (term acceptance_cap: the per-WMBT ceiling on acceptances; values.max = 5). Count > 5 is a finding.
Ratios: acceptance_to_test 1:1 (one acceptance -> one test); test_to_component N:1.
Each acceptance maps to exactly one metric_id (no mixed measures).
WMBT rules: one dimension and one lens_ref per WMBT; acceptances inherit context from the parent WMBT.
The count>5 finding signals only the cap violation; the ratio, metric_id and dimension/lens/context checks apply to every WMBT/acceptance regardless of count.

additions.text: S009-S012 are independent obligations (test ratio, single metric_id, WMBT dimension/lens); kept in prefer/avoid/verifier_detail and proposed as separate conventions in splitSuggestion.
Gaming the cap by merging independent checks into one compound acceptance.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming guard required by the authoring rules; consistent with the source's 'no mixed measures' and 1:1 acceptance-to-test ratio.

additions.text: Engineering reason phrased from the source statement ('split the WMBT into clearer outcomes'); the source has no explicit rationale field.
The count>5 finding signals only the cap violation; other retained checks apply regardless of count.
additions.justification: Clarifies activation scope so the retained S009-S012 requirements are not suppressed when the count is <=5.
